title: Storm-copied Spreading Insurrection into Goblin Bombardment

you: Goblin token 1 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Goblin token 2 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Mountain x5 (all tapped to cast Spreading Insurrection)

scenario.mana_available: {0} (the {4}{R} to cast Spreading Insurrection is already paid; no other mana source)

stack.note: cast as the third spell this turn; two spells were cast before it, so storm makes two copies

extras.note_for_the_resolver: Opponent creatures A-C are generic nontoken creatures with no relevant abilities.
extras.timing: It is your precombat main phase, you are the active player, and the stack was empty when you cast Spreading Insurrection (cost {4}{R}, already paid). It has just become cast and is on the stack.

scenario.question: Spreading Insurrection is cast as the third spell this turn, targeting Opponent creature A. Storm copies it twice; each copy targets a different opponent creature. After all resolve, can you sacrifice the three stolen creatures to Goblin Bombardment, and how much damage does that deal? Who owns and where do the sacrificed creatures go?

steps.action: Spreading Insurrection (original) is on the stack: cast from hand in your precombat main phase, as the active player, with the stack empty, as the third spell this turn, targeting Opponent creature A. Five Mountains were tapped to pay {4}{R}.
steps.effect: Sorcery timing is satisfied (your main phase, your turn, empty stack), which also fixes you as the active player for every later priority step (117.3b). The target is legal: A is a creature you don't control. Zada, Hedron Grinder's ability does NOT trigger: it triggers on an instant or sorcery that targets only Zada, and this spell targets an opponent's creature, so the event does not match.

steps.action: With the stack empty and priority, you activate Goblin Bombardment three times, sacrificing A, B and C as the costs, each activation targeting the opponent.
steps.effect: Legal: the activation follows the casting steps, including 601.2h cost payment (602.2b), and you control the stolen creatures, and only a permanent you control can be sacrificed. Bombardment's cost has no tap symbol, so the summoning-sickness rule is irrelevant (haste is not even needed). You retain priority after each activation, so all three can be stacked. Each sacrificed creature goes to its OWNER's graveyard — the opponent's — not yours. Each ability targets 'any target', which includes a player.

steps.effect: Each deals 1 damage to the opponent, who loses 1 life per damage: 3 damage total, opponent 20 -> 17. The sacrificed creatures are new objects in the opponent's graveyard; the 'until end of turn' control effects have nothing left to apply to.

final_state.summary: Yes. Storm makes two copies (two spells cast before it); copies retargeted to B and C, original keeps A; all three resolve and you control A, B, C until end of turn. Zada does not trigger (the spell does not target only Zada; copies are not cast). Sacrificing the three stolen creatures to Goblin Bombardment is legal (you control them; no tap cost) and deals 3 damage: opponent 20 -> 17. The creatures go to their owner's (the opponent's) graveyard. Spreading Insurrection goes to your graveyard; the copies cease to exist.

findings.note: NEW (prior missing-step finding FIXED). Full text: 'A player who has priority may cast a sorcery card from their hand during a main phase of their turn when the stack is empty.' Spreading Insurrection is a Sorcery (cards.json); extras.timing states precombat main, active player, empty stack. 'Of their turn' makes the caster the active player, which grounds the later 117.3b claims.
Target chosen on cast; A fits 'target creature you don't control' (oracle).

Zada triggers only on a spell that targets only Zada; no match. Consistent with Zada ruling 2018-03-16: 'Zada's ability triggers whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell that targets only Zada and no other object or player.'
Two spells cast before it -> two copies; new targets allowed. Printed reminder 'each spell cast before it' is equivalent to CR 'each other spell'.
Full text puts waiting triggers on the stack after the SBA check, before a player gets priority.
New targets B and C are legal. Agrees with ruling 2021-06-18 ('You can make different choices for each copy').
'a copy of a spell isn't cast' -> no storm/Zada trigger from copies. Agrees with rulings 2021-06-18 ('They aren't cast and won't be counted by other spells with storm') and Zada 2018-03-16.
Copy controlled (and, per the same rule, owned) by you.
Now grounded: step 1 establishes you are the active player via 307.1.
Full text 'Only tapped permanents can be untapped' matches the stated no-op on an untapped creature.
Copy goes to its owner's (your) graveyard per 707.10 ownership, then 704.5e.
A is still controlled by the opponent at resolution, so still a legal 'creature you don't control'.
You own the card -> your graveyard.
Controller activates; Bombardment is yours.

PRIOR FINDING FIXED. Full text: 'The remainder of the process for activating an ability is identical to the process for casting a spell listed in rules 601.2b-i ... An activated ability's analog to a spell's mana cost (as referenced in rule 601.2f) is its activation cost.' Brings 601.2h (and 601.2c target choice) into the activation.
PRIOR FINDING FIXED: now reached through 602.2b. 'Sacrifice a creature' is the total cost, paid in full.
Controller sacrifices; to OWNER's graveyard; cannot sacrifice what you don't control. Establishes both legality and destination.
A-C are nontoken (extras), so owner = card's owner = opponent.
Only tap/untap-symbol abilities of the creature itself; Bombardment's cost has neither. Correctly used to dismiss haste.
'any target' includes players.
3 damage, single opponent: 20 -> 17. Per-seat and pod total coincide (scenario-facts: 1 opponent, 20 life).

Note (not failing): the 'not asked' extension sacrifices Zada; if done, 903.9a (commander to command zone, an SBA) would apply, so 'no other state-based action applies' is true only of the main line. The 6-damage / 14-life arithmetic is unaffected and follows from step 7's 602.2/701.21a.
